# Lionheart Fixt 0.39.0 - the Enchanter's Bargain

There's a well in La Calle Perdida most players never open. Down it is a mad necromancer who has
spent an age collecting the souls of everyone who ever fell into his prison.

The original game lets you do two things about him: kill him, or talk him into destroying himself.
Both pay you. There is a third thing you can do — talk him down and let him live — and it pays
**nothing at all**.

This release pays it, and connects him to the one other person in the game who would want what
he has.

## He's already Relican

Here's the thing that made this release feel found rather than invented.

The Mad Enchanter uses **Lord Relican's character model, Relican's stats, and Relican's spells**.
They are the only two characters in the whole game built that way — one shared asset between the
Arch Necromancer of the Dark Wielders and the madman in the bottle.

Nobody ever wrote the connection down. It's in the artwork and the numbers and nowhere in the
script.

The script does reach for it once. If your Barter is good enough, you can tell him you'll bring
him *more* spirits — and he actually considers it, and lets you live to see if you meant it. Then
nothing happens, because there was never any way to deliver on the offer.

Now there is.

## What you can do

| if you... | you get |
|---|---|
| **kill him** | Kublai Khan's Sword and gold — exactly as before |
| **spare him** | the **Amulet of the Trapped Spirit** |
| **hand him to Relican** | the **Ring** as well, a bonus for wearing both, and he arms your sceptre |

Sparing him is not a skill check. I expected to find it locked behind a high Speech score and it
isn't — **any character can talk him down**, at any level. You convince him that the souls he's
been hoarding hold enough power to charge the crystal he built before he lost his mind. Just don't
tell him to his face that he lost his mind. He takes that badly.

The two items are a matched pair: the amulet carries mana and turns aside hostile magic, the ring
sharpens the kinds of magic he practised, and wearing both is worth more than wearing them one at
a time.

## The Dark Wielders were missing a step

If you join the Wielders, you earn the spirit in your wand. You fetch the darkwood, Cedric shapes
it into an empty rod, and then there's a whole quest — Galileo, the Observatory — about finding a
soul to put in it.

If you join the **Dark** Wielders, the equivalent sceptre just turns up finished.

The empty version exists. It's in the game files, with its own description: *"Fashioned darkwood
that is but an empty shell without a spirit to power it."* Nothing in the game ever gives it to
you.

So now DaVinci's secret chamber gives you the empty one, and you need a soul for it — and you
happen to know a man with a cellar full of them.

**If you killed the Enchanter, or never found the well, Relican will do it himself.** He's an Arch
Necromancer with a wraith on call; this is beneath him but not beyond him. The quest can't get
stuck.

## The evil ending finally has a name

If you side with Relican and destroy La Calle Perdida, the game already took it seriously: a
colossal karma hit, three quests failed, Cedric told what you did.

But the title written for that ending — **"Dark Lord of Calle Perdida"** — was never awarded to
anyone. The text describes exactly what you did, word for word, and nothing in the game handed it
over. The Inquisition's version of the same betrayal *does* get its title. The dark one didn't.

Now it does.

## And a cheat I closed

Worth saying plainly, because it's in the game you bought.

The Sceptre of Bone gave you skill points **every time you picked it up**, and never took them
away. Drop it, pick it up, and you're permanently better at magic. Repeat as desired. Forever.

It now works like every other piece of gear in the game: the bonus applies while you're holding
it, and stops when you aren't.

## Installing

Unzip and double-click **`Mod Manager.bat`**, then click the button that names the mod.

Works on **any save** — but the new content is in La Calle Perdida and the plane below it, so a
save that has already been through there won't show it.

## If you play it

**The check that matters most:** if you're on Relican's path, take the sceptre from DaVinci's
chamber, then kill the Enchanter, then go talk to Relican. He must offer to fill the sceptre
himself. If that option isn't there, the Dark Wielder questline can't be finished and I need to
know immediately.

**The fun one:** equip the Sceptre of Bone, write down your Thought and Tribal skills, then drop
it and pick it up five times. Nothing should change. In the original game you'd be ten points
better off.

**And the honest warning:** the Dark Wielder path has never been played, by me or anyone else I
know of. This release adds to a questline that was already untested ground.
